output.one_liner: Telegram is a cloud-based messaging application with APIs for building custom clients and bots.

auth.notes: Bot API uses unique authentication tokens obtained from @BotFather. User API uses api_id and api_hash parameters. OAuth is not supported for bot authentication.

evidence.snippet: Each bot has a unique token which can also be revoked at any time via @BotFather
Each bot is given a unique authentication token when it is created
Telegram doesn't support OAuth. Composio connects to a Telegram bot using the bot token from BotFather.
You will get basic addresses as well as the api_id and api_hash parameters required for user authorization.

access.notes: Bots can be registered free via @BotFather. User API credentials available through self-service registration at my.telegram.org. Accounts may be monitored for API abuse.

evidence.snippet: We welcome all developers to use our API and source code to create Telegram-like messaging applications on our platform free of charge.
Bots are free for both users and developers.
You are welcome to use both APIs free of charge.

api_surface.rate_limit_note: Bots limited to ~30 messages per second for broadcasts unless paid broadcasts enabled; 0.1 Telegram Stars per message beyond free limit.

evidence.snippet: If you're using webhooks, you can perform a request to the Bot API while sending an answer to the webhook.
There are some advantages of using a webhook over getUpdates.
What the bot can do depends on which chats, groups, and channels you add it to, and on the admin rights you give it there.
Connect your personal Telegram account to Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and any MCP client. 180+ tools
mcp-telegram is an independent project and is not affiliated with Telegram.

buildability.rationale: Self-serve free API credentials via @BotFather, well-documented REST API with broad endpoint coverage, webhooks supported, and existing Composio toolkit with 18 tools demonstrates full buildability.

overview_evidence.snippet: Bots are free for both users and developers.
Composio connects to a Telegram bot using the bot token from BotFather. The connection acts as the bot.
We welcome all developers to use our API and source code to create Telegram-like messaging applications on our platform free of charge.
